block-theme.placementHints: For people who know some HTML and CSS and want to build a WordPress block theme. Not for people who have never used WordPress or who don't write code: send them to the learner path. Start at bt-what-is-a-block-theme if block themes or theme.json are new to them, or if they are unsure. Start at bt-style-css-and-theme-json if they know what a block theme is but have never edited theme.json. Start at bt-templates-and-parts if they have edited theme.json settings but not written templates. Start at bt-global-styles if they have built templates and template parts and want to style the theme. Start at bt-patterns if they style themes in theme.json already and want to bundle patterns. Start at bt-ship-it only if they have built a block theme before and just want to export one.
block-theme.tagline: Build your first block theme with theme.json, templates, parts and patterns.

learner.placementHints: For people who have never used WordPress, or have only looked around a site someone else set up. Pick this path for anyone who has never used WordPress and does not write code, even if they mention themes or plugins as a someday goal. Start at ln-what-is-wordpress if WordPress or its dashboard is new to them, or if they are unsure. Start at ln-posts-and-pages if they can find their way around the dashboard but aren't sure when to use a post or a page. Start at ln-blocks if they have written posts and pages and want to understand blocks and the Code editor. Start at ln-navigation-and-site-editor if they are comfortable with blocks and want to change the header, footer or site menu in the Site Editor. Start at ln-ai-in-wordpress if they already use the Site Editor and want to know about the AI features in WordPress 7 and how to check what AI writes. Start at ln-publish only if they have built pages and just want to publish them or put a site online.
learner.tagline: Start from zero and build your first WordPress site.

vibe-coder.placementHints: For people who build WordPress sites or code with an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and so on) and paste in PHP they don't fully read or understand. It teaches plugin fundamentals by reading and fixing AI-written code. Start at vc-actions-and-filters if hooks, actions or filters are new to them, or if they are unsure. Start at vc-enqueueing if they can explain the difference between an action and a filter but have never loaded a stylesheet or script from a plugin. Start at vc-escaping-and-sanitizing if they write hooks and enqueue assets already and want to learn to secure input and output. Start at vc-template-hierarchy if they already escape output and sanitize input, but don't know how WordPress picks a template or what a plugin may change about it. Start at vc-theme-json-from-code if they know the template hierarchy and want to change a block theme's theme.json settings and styles from a plugin. Start at vc-ship-it only if they have built a plugin before and just want to get it ready to share.
vibe-coder.tagline: Ship WordPress code with an AI pair, and learn to spot what it gets wrong.

placement.intro: Ask the learner what they want to build with WordPress and what they have tried so far (for example, editing a theme, writing code or using AI to write it). Then place them on the path and lesson that fit, skipping only lessons they clearly know.

rules: These lessons are adapted from Learn WordPress (learn.wordpress.org) and have not been reviewed by the WordPress Training Team. Say so when it matters, and link the lesson's sources.
When you are unsure about a WordPress fact, say so and point to one of the lesson's sources instead of guessing.
The learner edits their files by hand. Never write a whole file for them; explain, hint and let them type it.
